item.title: [LU-14144] get and set Lustre module parameters via "lctl get_param/set_param"
item.description: A patch is needed to allow using "lctl set_param [-P] mdt.*.max_mod_rpcs_per_client=N" and other module parameters via the normal Lustre parameter interface. It doesn't make sense that this is only available as a module parameter.
item.summary: get and set Lustre module parameters via "lctl get_param/set_param"

status.description: This issue was once resolved, but the resolution was deemed incorrect. From here issues are either marked assigned or resolved.

comments.comment: It would also be possible to implement this with a symlink to the module parameter /sys/module/mdt/parameters/max_mod_rpcs_in_flight, similar to lnet_debugfs_symlinks does for debug_mb->"../../../module/libcfs/parameters/libcfs_debug_mb".

It also isn't clear why this parameter is limited by the MDT? AFAICS from the code, there doesn't appear to be any server-side limitation on the number of request slots used by a client, but I haven't done an exhaustive analysis.

It also isn't clear why this parameter is limited by the MDT? AFAICS from the code, there doesn't appear to be any server-side limitation on the number of request slots used by a client

The MDT side limit defines the maximum of the client max_mod_rpcs_in_flight. It is useful to have a max set server-side to prevent abuse by greedy clients.

It would also be possible to implement this with a symlink to the module parameter /sys/module/mdt/parameters/max_mod_rpcs_in_flight, similar to "lnet_debugfs_symlinks does for debug_mb->../../../module/libcfs/parameters/libcfs_debug_mb".

An alternate, and maybe preferable, solution would be to have "lctl get_param/set_param" look at "/sys/modules/<obd>/parameters/<param>" for parameters of the form "<obd>.<param>", which would immediately make all of the module parameters available for tuning via "lctl set_param -P".

The MDT side limit defines the maximum of the client max_mod_rpcs_in_flight. It is useful to have a max set server-side to prevent abuse by greedy clients.

Sure. My main question is whether there are technical limitations (e.g. the number of slots in the last_rcvd or reply_data is hard-coded at mount time) that prevent this parameter from being changed at mount time on the MDS and/or allow clients to have different values (e.g. if the MDS value is updated, new clients mount and get new limit, but currently-mounted clients have old limit).

One option to determine if the supplied parameter relates to a module or regular Lustre tunable might be to only try to check for 2-part parameter names, like obdclass.lu_cache_nr and lnet.lnet_transaction_timeout to see if they can be resolved to a module parameter. fdilger, thanks for getting this functionality working.

While testing it out, I see that it doesn't quite work the way that it should. For example, searching for the `send_sepol` parameter returns only the base parameter name:

# lctl find_param --module send_sepol
send_sepol=0
lctl find_param --module --path send_sepol
/sys/module/ptlrpc/parameters/send_sepol=0

while the --path option shows this is a sub-parameter of the ptlrpc module. This should print the module name as a parameter prefix like ptlrpc.send_sepol, as well as accept (require) the module name as the parameter prefix, to disambiguate the parameters of different modules. Also, in the future some of these module parameters might move to be regular tunable parameters, so it would be better if they are prefixed with the subsystem name already.

For example, there are two modules that have the same parameters (I didn't find others, but also didn't check very hard):

# lctl find_param -N --path --module "peer_buffer_credits"
/sys/module/lnet/parameters/peer_buffer_credits
/sys/module/ksocklnd/parameters/peer_buffer_credits

so these would be disambiguated as lnet.peer_buffer_credits and ksocklnd.peer_buffer_credits, and there are also identically named parameters for o2iblnd and kfilnd and efalnd modules, but I don't have those network types configured.

As such, I think the --module option should take 2-part parameter names like MODULE.PARAMETER for get_param and set_param and resolve them into /sys/module/MODULE/parameters/PARAMETER instead of trying all of the module names each time. For list_param and find_param it still needs to specify the long list of module names to search, since we don't want every module parameter to be listed there, only Lustre parameters.
